question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x+C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (8x-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}})\text{d}x & =\int 8x\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\int x\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{x}^{2}-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+\frac{2}{1+{x}^{2}})\text{d}x & =\int x\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int x\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Integrating Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions and Some Manipulations
question.worked_solution:
This integral doesn't look like one of the basic ones. However, we can manipulate the numerator a bit  to make it look more like the denominator, which reveals a more familiar expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1} & =\frac{5{x}^{2}+5-5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{5({x}^{2}+1)-5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{5({x}^{2}+1)}{{x}^{2}+1}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{5\cancel{({x}^{2}+1)}}{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =5-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Remembering that

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x,
$$

we can now calculate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (5-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}+1})\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5x-5\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
